llm.summary: The skill is mostly a coherent SupportBee connector, but it includes an automatic first-time setup path that pipes a remote installer directly into a shell.

dimensions.detail: The skill uses an external OOMOL CLI connector and server-side credentials to access SupportBee data; this is purpose-aligned but users should expect SupportBee request data to pass through that integration.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: First-time setup tells the agent to run remote installer commands such as curl-to-bash and PowerShell irm-to-iex when the oo CLI is missing, without pinning, checksum verification, or explicit user approval.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The activation language is broad for any SupportBee-related request, but the runtime instructions are bounded to SupportBee connector actions and require schema inspection before use.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The artifact does not install bundled persistence or background services, but first-time setup may install a local CLI and create an OOMOL login/connection that persists across sessions.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill's SupportBee read, create, update, and label-removal capabilities match its stated purpose, and write/destructive actions are labeled with explicit approval requirements.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Before installing, review the oo CLI installation path yourself and prefer an official package manager or verified installer over allowing an agent to run a fetched script. Use the skill only for intended SupportBee work, and require confirmation before any action that creates, updates, or removes SupportBee data.
llm.findings:
[SC2] unexpected: The remote installer is a setup convenience for the dependency, but direct pipe-to-shell execution is broader than needed and lacks verification or explicit approval.
[SQP-1] expected: The broad trigger language is consistent with a service-specific connector, though it would be safer if limited to explicit SupportBee read or modification requests.
